summary.text: A 2-year-old South Asian girl presented with a 13-month history of progressive abdominal distention and intermittent fever. She had no trauma, gastrointestinal symptoms, other medical history or notable family history, and examination showed a large, hard, non-tender abdominal mass.

Ultrasound showed a large echogenic mid-abdominal mass without Doppler vascular supply, and contrast CT showed a well-circumscribed non-enhancing hypodense left abdominal mass of about 18.4 × 14.8 × 13.6 cm with fat-range Hounsfield units, internal septations and displacement of the left kidney, spleen and bowel. Laboratory tests were routine. Imaging favored lipoma or lipoblastoma, and malignant transformation could not be excluded.

She underwent laparotomy with complete resection and negative margins, and a regional lymph node was biopsied. The roughly 2 kg encapsulated fatty mass was confirmed on histopathology as a benign lipoma without atypia or necrosis, and the lymph node showed reactive hyperplasia without tumor invasion.

The postoperative period was uneventful with discharge on the fourth postoperative day, and she was asymptomatic at the 6-week follow-up; a second follow-up at 8 post-op months is listed as not occurred.
